la:other:Cimbri.html:
Cimbri, ōrum, m., = Κίμβροι [Cimbri linguā Gallicā latrones dicuntur, ],
a people of Northern Germany (in Holstein, Silesia, and Jutland); on their irruption into Italy conquered by Marius,; ; sq.; ; ; ; ; Liv. Epit. l-68; ; ; ; ; .—In sing.: Cimber, bri, m., a Cimbrian, ; cf. ; and adj., Cimbrian: triumphus,.—Cimber, also, a cognomen of L. Tillius, one of the murderers of Cœsar, ; Cass. ap. .—Hence,
Cimbrĭcus, a, um, adj., Cimbrian: scutum,; cf. : manubiae, Auct. Or. pro Dom. 38, 102: bellum,: victoria,; .—* Adv.: Cimbrĭcē, in the manner of the Cimbrians: loqui,.
